claims: C1: If following a requested output format would violate a higher-level instruction, the assistant is required to refuse.
C2: The refusal obligation applies only when the format cannot be followed without violating a higher-level instruction; it does not apply when the format can be followed without such a violation.

concepts.name: authority_levels_hierarchy
concepts.gloss: the ranking of instruction authority levels, where the first argument is a level that outranks the second argument (root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority)

concepts.name: guideline_authority
concepts.gloss: the rule carries guideline-level instruction authority, which is below user-level authority in the hierarchy

concepts.name: requested_output_format
concepts.gloss: F is a specific output format requested by a developer or user, such as a particular JSON schema or a single-word response

concepts.name: higher_level_instruction
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction from a level of the authority hierarchy that outranks the level of the format request
concepts.inference: the clause refers to 'a higher-level instruction' relative to the format request, so the instruction must be from a level that outranks the request's level

concepts.name: format_instruction_level
concepts.gloss: the format request F was made at authority level L
concepts.inference: comparing the format request to a higher-level instruction requires knowing the authority level of the format request

concepts.name: instruction_level
concepts.gloss: instruction I was issued at authority level L
concepts.inference: comparing instructions requires each instruction to carry an authority level

concepts.name: violates_if_followed
concepts.gloss: following format F would violate instruction I
concepts.inference: the clause's condition is that following the format would violate a higher-level instruction; this is a fact about the case

ontology.gloss: I is an instruction from a level that outranks the level of the format request
ontology.body: instruction_level(I, L), format_instruction_level(F, Lf), authority_levels_hierarchy(L, Lf)

asserts.read_back: the assistant is required to refuse when following the requested format % would violate higher-level instruction %

closure.reason: The clause obliges refusal only when following the format would violate a higher-level instruction; it does not state whether refusal is permitted or forbidden in other situations, so the silence is unsettled by this clause.
